title: Siege of Damascus begins
description: Fifteen days after the reverse of Merj as-Soffar, the Muslim army began the siege of Damascus, the Capital of Syria, on the 16th of Moharram AH 14. The Arabs had no experience of besieging walled towns, and Khalid had to summon Shurahbil from the Jordan province and 'Amr from Palestine to his aid. Khalid's division faced the East Gate, Abu 'Obeida the Gate of Jabiya, Yezid the Bab as-Saghir, 'Amr the Bab Tuma and Shurahbil the River Gate, so the City was completely surrounded.

sources.citation: Sir William Muir, The Caliphate: Its Rise, Decline, and Fall, "CHAPTER XIII"
